ops.title: terminalOutcomeDigest is not a durable format — the struct it hashes is free to change
ops.body:
Verdict (2026-08-03, daemonkit v0.21 migration): changing the struct hashed by
`terminalOutcomeDigest` (`internal/accountterminal/terminal.go`, ~:1435) is NOT a
durable-format break. No path recomputes a terminal outcome digest from live
state and compares it against a stored one.

This was gating: the v0.21 migration retypes `proc.Record`, which is one of the
four fields hashed (`{kind, exit_code, signal, record}`). Two lanes checked it
independently and a third pass confirmed. Recording it so the next person to
touch that struct does not re-derive it.

## The structural proof (strongest form)

`internal/accountterminal` imports exactly ONE external package —
`github.com/yasyf/daemonkit/proc` (post-migration: daemonkit's root only). No
store, no journal, no durable, no encoding package. The package cannot persist
anything, so no call-site census is needed to rule out a durable break: it is
unrepresentable. This argument survives future edits in a way an enumeration
does not — re-verify it by checking the import block, not by re-walking callers.

## The trap: `outcome_digest` is a NAME COLLISION

The persisted `outcome_digest` column (`internal/store/store.go`, receipt field
`internal/store/account_mutation.go:135`) is a DIFFERENT digest. It is typed
`store.CredentialDigest` and covers credential state, not terminal outcome.
Every daemon write site passes `ExpectedCredentialDigest` or `state.Digest()`
(`internal/daemon/account_mutation.go:181,664,1222,1249`), and the store's
recompute-and-compare paths (`internal/store/account_mutation.go:1011,1018,
1128-1133`) recompute from credential `Observation.Digest()`.
`TerminalOutcome.Digest` never flows into the store.

Reading the column name as "the terminal outcome's digest" is the single most
likely way to get this question wrong, in either direction.

## Supporting facts

- Computed once at settlement (`terminal.go:1219`), stored only in the in-memory
  `t.result` (:1221). `t.result` is never serialized.
- Only comparison is `Acknowledge` (`terminal.go:936`) against a caller-echoed
  copy. The single non-test caller is `internal/daemon/account_mutation.go:62`,
  echoing a value it got from `Wait` in the same process. Terminal outcomes do
  not survive daemon restart, so an old-format and a new-format digest can never
  meet.
- Never on the wire: `internal/daemon/protocol.go` carries only
  `store.CredentialDigest` fields.
- Zero golden/testdata files in the repo. `TestTerminalOutcomeDigestBindsCompleteRecord`
  (`internal/accountterminal/terminal_test.go:522`) is a SENSITIVITY test — two
  records must hash differently — not a golden pin, so it survives a format
  change and is evidence in neither direction.
- The v0.20.9 goldens in `internal/store/upgrade_fixture_test.go` pin
  `owner_record` bytes, unrelated to this digest.

## What would invalidate this

Any of: `internal/accountterminal` growing an import that can write to disk or
encode for the wire; `TerminalOutcome.Digest` being added to a protocol message;
terminal state being made to survive a daemon restart. Re-check the import block
first — it is the cheapest signal.
